I'm a 52-year-old woman who's been farming these lands in Quzhou for over thirty years. I only went to primary school, but I know my fields. Every year I stick to what works — the wheat-maize double crop. My family has about 8 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. The wheat went in last October, and now that spring has come I need to topdress it with fertilizer and start irrigating. After we harvest the wheat in early June, I'll plant maize the same day — no need to plough, just sow straight into the stubble. That's what everyone here does, and it saves time and diesel.

I buy improved wheat seed — Luyuan502 has done well for me — and hybrid maize seed, Denghai605. The hybrids yield more, and the seed dealer is right in town. For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer when I plant, and then topdress with urea when the wheat greens up and again when the maize is knee-high. I don't fuss with soil tests; I apply what my neighbors apply and what I've always applied. I irrigate three times for wheat and twice for maize — the groundwater is still decent here. I spray for insects and weeds two or three times each crop. Rotary tillage for wheat, no-tillage for maize. I don't grow cotton anymore — too many pesticide sprays and the labor is hard on my back. I need reliable food and income, not gambling on fancy crops.
